newsitem.title: USA: NYPA hikes daily, non-firm power transmission rate.
newsitem.headline: NYPA hikes daily, non-firm power transmission rate.

text.p: The New York Power Authority (NYPA), after one postponement, said Friday it is more than doubling the price it charges to move daily, non-firm electricity on its transmission system.
The new fee, to take effect from 0001 EST Monday, raises the price to $6.43 per megawatt hour from $3.00 previously.
"We're definitely going to start on Monday," said NYPA spokesman Ira Fine.
The new rate is part of NYPA's transmission plan to comply with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) open transmission policy.
The policy gives all energy suppliers equal access to NYPA and other utilities' high-voltage lines and other transmission services as a way to increase competition.
NYPA delayed implementing the new rate by a month to give electricity traders and schedulers more time to adjust to the higher fee.
While NYPA's new daily, non-firm transmission price more than doubled its old rate, its transmission charge for a longer period is considerably lower, Fine said.
NYPA's new, non-firm wire fee for a full week, 24-hours day, will be $3.04/MWh from Monday.
